req_time_temple_season_shop.evidence: no call site: the name only exists in TimeTempleCmd.lua prototype 6

clientSendPath.evidence: prototype 8 builds TimeTempleCmd as name -> encoder closure; prototypes 0-7 call Codec.EncodeErl (7 names) and Codec.EncodePB(pb_time_temple_select_runes_skills) for skill select. No numeric type appears anywhere in the module.
prototype 5 (Seq:Send) pc 0-5: NetMgr.GetSession(NetMgr.GAME_LOGIC_SESSION):SendMsg(cmd, callback, args...); cmd stays the string name.
prototype 8 (Session:SendMsg) gates on state and forwards to self._con:Send(cmd, ...).

prototype 3 (Connection:Send) pc 41-45: type = Cmd.c2s_index[cmd]; IST on the result, and when it is nil the function calls error("send msg type error") and returns before encoding pb_c2s. This is the only place a request name becomes a wire type.
prototype 21 (Connection:_HandReqCallback) pc 10-15: the reply is decoded with Cmd.c2s_back[cmd], so a request without a c2s_back entry could not be decoded even if a server answered it.
prototype 5 formats the same-frame duplicate warning as "cmd:%s", confirming the value passed to Send is the string name.
txt_Cmd_lua -> "Cmd.lua.txt" is the only command table asset; there is no second downloaded registry.

conclusion: The client cannot emit these eight requests in this build. Cmd.lua exposes exactly one request registry (c2s_index, 1407 names) and none of the eight req_time_temple_* names is present in c2s_index, c2s_back or c2s_switch. Connection:Send resolves the wire type from c2s_index and aborts on a miss, so no numeric C2S type exists to recover and the time temple UI path cannot reach the server. The numeric type was therefore not recovered as "hard to find"; it is absent from the shipped client command table.
limitations: This is a negative result for client build 1.55.090365 only. A later client release (or a hot-updated command table) could register these names with types that cannot be derived from this artifact.
The module still ships its UI, config and protobuf schemas, and the server side (module 159 login, S2C 7801 push) is unchanged, so a future client may need these handlers.
Static bytecode only: no client Lua was executed and no game traffic was produced for this evidence.
